projects.name: Bank VaR: LSTM vs GARCH
projects.stat: Retrained yearly, the LSTM matched GARCH's accuracy (15 breaks, every test passed) with about 10% less capital.
title: Bank
VaR
projects.label: Market risk model · MGSC 673
projects.intro: Three ways to forecast a bank's worst day: Historical Simulation, GARCH and an LSTM. I built all three for a Canadian bank trading book and backtested them against Basel rules from 2022 to 2026.

problem.text: Banks set aside capital based on their Value-at-Risk. The industry default, Historical Simulation, only looks at last year, so it reacts to a new crisis weeks late and the regulator penalises it.
problem.highlight: reacts to a new crisis weeks late

highlights.title: A trading book built from public data
highlights.text: Daily prices for the Big Five banks, the TSX, bonds, Canadian yields, VIX and USD/CAD from 2007 to 2026: 4,957 trading days. The portfolio covers equity, rate and FX risk in one book.

highlights.title: An LSTM that predicts volatility, then calibrates the tail
highlights.text: 60-day input sequences feed an LSTM(64) that outputs one volatility forecast. Real tails are fatter than a bell curve, so I replaced the normal multiplier (2.33) with one calibrated on validation data (2.81).

highlights.title: Retrained every year, like a real bank would
highlights.text: Seven of the LSTM's 17 misses fell in 2026, eight years after its training data ended. Yearly walk-forward retraining cut 2026 misses from 7 to 4 and lifted the capital saving from 7% to 12%.

highlights.title: A dashboard anyone can test
highlights.text: Pick a model and a period, then drag a what-if buffer to see breaks, the traffic light and capital recompute live. At a buffer of 1.0, every number matches the report.

stats.title: As accurate as GARCH
stats.text: Both retrained models broke 15 times on 1,212 test days and passed the Kupiec and Christoffersen tests.

stats.title: Less capital
stats.text: The LSTM's average capital charge was 3.92% of the portfolio against 4.36% for GARCH.

stats.title: Days in the yellow zone
stats.text: The trade-off: more days on watch with the regulator, and misses that follow calm markets.

overview: Data pipeline, models, backtesting and the interactive dashboard
Yahoo Finance, Bank of Canada, FRED
Historical Simulation, GARCH(1,1), LSTM, Kupiec and Christoffersen tests, Basel traffic light
deliverables: Walk-forward retraining for both GARCH and LSTM
tech: Split
Train 2007–2018, validation 2019–2021, test 2022–2026. Scaler fitted on train only.
Features
Portfolio return, 20-day volatility, VIX, yield change, USD/CAD return, TSX return.
LSTM
60-day sequences → LSTM(64) → dropout 0.2 → log-variance. Gaussian negative log-likelihood, Adam, early stopping.
Evaluation
Break counts, Kupiec and Christoffersen tests, Basel traffic light, capital = max(VaR, k × 60-day average VaR).
What I'd do next
A VaR floor for calm markets, 10 seeds instead of 3, and a rates-heavy portfolio preset.
projects.note: The dashboard previews use illustrative data; every number in the text, tiles at rest and bar charts comes from the project's backtest.

breaks.title: Breaks on 1,212 test days, 2022–2026
breaks.caption: A break is a day the loss beat the VaR forecast. About 12 are expected.

capital.title: Average capital charge, % of portfolio
capital.caption: Lower is cheaper for the bank, as long as the model stays accurate.

projects.name: LLM Game for Deaf Students
projects.stat: Engaged students scored significantly higher than control (p = .022, η²p = .549).
title: Signs
& words
projects.label: Thesis · Published in IEEE 2026
projects.intro: A game-based English learning system for Thai deaf students, with LLM feedback, Thai translation and Thai Sign Language support. Tested in a controlled trial with 62 students.

problem.text: Deaf students in Thailand learn English as a third language, after Thai Sign Language and written Thai. Many in grades 9 to 12 read English at a grade 6 level, and most teaching tools rely on sound.
problem.highlight: read English at a grade 6 level

highlights.title: Three games, five levels each
highlights.text: Word Choice, Jumble and Matching follow the order people learn language in: vocabulary, then word order, then meaning. Levels alternate new content with review.

highlights.title: Feedback in the student's own languages
highlights.text: Gemini 2.5 Flash writes simple hints in English and Thai. 3D pose estimation turns sign language videos into an animated signer. An LLM-as-a-judge test picked Gemini over GPT-4o Mini (4.08 vs 3.68).

media.alt: Feedback screens in English and Thai

highlights.title: A controlled trial at a school for the deaf
highlights.text: 62 students, 30 sessions of 20 minutes each. For students who attended at least 70% of sessions, scores improved significantly over the control group.

stats.title: Students in the trial
stats.text: Grades 9 to 12 at Setsatian School for the Deaf, split into control and intervention groups.

stats.title: Large effect
stats.text: Among engaged students, adjusted scores were 9.47 against 5.65 for control (p = .022).

stats.title: Feedback quality
stats.text: Gemini 2.5 Flash's score out of 5 for accuracy, tone and clarity, rated by an LLM judge.

overview: Bachelor's thesis, published in IEEE conference proceedings, 2026
System design, LLM integration, trial analysis
Gemini 2.5 Flash, RAG, 3D pose estimation, game app
Randomised controlled trial, ANCOVA, intention-to-treat and per-protocol analysis
deliverables: LLM feedback in English and Thai
tech: Curriculum
Thai core curriculum, grade 6 (CEFR A1): vocabulary, plurals, articles, prepositions, four tenses.
Design
Vivid colours, pixel graphics, minimal text, 20-minute sessions.
Analysis
ITT (n = 50) showed no overall effect; PP (n = 12, ≥70% attendance) showed a large effect.

projects.name: BreathMo® ECMO Market Entry
projects.stat: ฿230M addressable market, 52.81% IRR, break-even in year 3.
title: ECMO
for Thailand
projects.label: Market entry strategy · Business pitch
projects.intro: A go-to-market plan for bringing a locally supported ECMO heart-lung system to Thai hospitals, from market sizing to a four-year financial model.

problem.text: ECMO keeps critically ill patients alive, but in Thailand the machines are imported, expensive and come with no local support, so many hospitals that need them don't have one.
problem.highlight: imported, expensive and come with no local support

highlights.title: Sizing the market from case counts
highlights.text: TAM, SAM and SOM built from hospital data, ECMO case counts (300 to 500 a year, growing 10 to 30%) and demand forecasts.

highlights.title: Who to sell to first
highlights.text: 20+ hospitals identified and split into tiers: Bangkok teaching hospitals in year one, then four regions.

highlights.title: A four-year financial model
highlights.text: Revenue, costs and returns with sensitivity analysis. The plan breaks even in year 3.

stats.title: Addressable market
stats.text: With a ฿18M serviceable target in year one.

stats.title: IRR
stats.text: With a ฿7.3M NPV over four years.

stats.title: Break-even
stats.text: Direct B2B sales through hospitals, conferences and outreach.

overview: Market research, competitor analysis, financial model, pitch
TAM-SAM-SOM, feature-price comparison, stakeholder interviews, NPV/IRR
tech: Lessons
Market sizing assumptions compound into projections. Healthcare sales need clinicians, administrators and procurement on board at once.

projects.name: Orthodontic Wire FEA
projects.stat: Low-grade wire was stiffer (13.18 vs 9.39 GPa) with up to 3× the stress concentration.
title: Wire
under stress
projects.label: Biomechanics · EGBI 261
projects.intro: Do cheap orthodontic wires move teeth the same way as standard ones? I tested both in the lab and simulated them on a 3D model of a dental arch.

problem.text: Low-quality orthodontic wires are common where regulation is weak. They can deliver force unpredictably, which puts tooth movement and patient safety at risk.

highlights.title: Tensile tests on both wires
highlights.text: Three samples of each wire, stress-strain curves and Young's modulus for each.

highlights.title: A 3D dental arch in CAD
highlights.text: Teeth, gum, periodontal ligament, brackets and wire, modelled and assembled for simulation.

media.alt: CAD model of the dental arch

highlights.title: Finite element analysis in Ansys
highlights.text: Material data from the lab went into Ansys Workbench. Low-quality wire showed stress hotspots up to 3× higher.

stats.title: Stiffer, less elastic
stats.text: Low-grade wire against 9.39 GPa for standard nitinol.

stats.title: Stress concentration
stats.text: Hotspots that raise the risk of root resorption.

stats.title: Wire samples tested
stats.text: Three of each type, tested to failure.

tech: Setup
Fixed supports at bone anchors, horizontal forces for wire-induced movement, refined mesh.
